title: Information
text:
Note



This one is taken as demonstrating example for the template. For the original, see RHINELAB@MTAIL for the specific details.


While most of the contents of this page centred around the main works, research and observations realized in operation, it is fairly necessary to also outlines what are to be of the motivation, condition of existence, our philosophies and what to believe in. Furthermore, it is also the concentrated analysis that we would have to make, in dealing with any given scientific pursuit, any form of novelty and research, and any process of dealing with experimental-theoretical propositions, in the case we should not make it sounds like a bunch of crackpots.
Nominally, RHINE-MTAIL is the core splinter group, under direct and incorporated control of the main laboratory, RHINELAB (or RINALAB, as the second name), focus on delivering and outlining the work mode operation of subsequent components, governance models and analysis during its operation, a large portion of modelling-theoretic theory of science, which simply means we treat science, largely initiated of this line of thinking from Kuhnian cycle, to be a system of model, arbitrary given 1, and is capable to be changed, diluted 2, deferred 3, and so on. One of the main goal in such regard is to diagnose the structure, and to see the failure point, as if nothing is seen or recognized, nothing can even be done. That is why you would see the initial idea when MTAIL was formed, is to create the ordering level of fundamentality, from CI to CIII, respectively.
1 If pushed far enough, this central view admits that even mathematics is under scrutiny as for it to be also, a model - a very good one that a lot used it for.2 When a theory is operated upon, there exists the risk, or rather the inevitability of it reaching further out, thus diluting the main framework into a proliferated view of different applications, different apparatus and contexts, and so on. Another notion that also falls into this umbrella is when heuristics are too much and dilute the field of its central tenet, and thus make it so to be an in-depth dilution, both in the stacks that every heuristic and empirical claims have made, and in the depth of the dependency track follows.3 When a theory fails something, or in contest, it usually defers the topic into unsolvable, claiming of correctness and reevaluation of such problem of its existence, projecting to correct one problem in opposition while laying out severals, or defers directly the problem as a special case, perhaps.Aside from such governing role that feeds into the philosophy and operational mode of RHINELAB itself, the subject of MTAIL is pointed, and foundational in its core. The main subject of the lab includes several ‘doctrines’, each of which can be considered or thought of as specific analytical views, subject of studies and expansion, or analytical direction on many fields (basically means the posture and the upper-theoretical that would be applied or stationed when working on particular fields). Some of them are about artificial intelligence, some of them are about theoretical research, such as pure mathematics, theoretical physics and the contact with non-pure, applied sections. Some of them are about the thesis of a more foundational stack, i.e. mathematical modelling and the entirety of modelling theory in full, information theory and adjacent arguments.
Perhaps, before we list them in details of the philosophy and what to cover thereof, we can think of the central research of MTAIL as the scientific rigorous framework itself - concerning of all relevant topics, of all load-bearing foundational field or systems, and the extension thereof. It is really hard to say without committing to any specific form of framework, because those contain their own bias or structural views, of which all can be considered a piece of reality or the actual substance itself. Thus, in a sense, MTAIL’s interest, even if the topic and starting point varies, all point to a singular thread - the deepest possible investigation and research of the bodies of (rigorous) theoretical-empirical studies, and their connections to the realized world 4. And lastly, the research on which to diagnose the cost of everything - of the move from theory to practice, of practical to what is written, of where to which, of what to whom, all of which contingent and hidden under decisions and discourses of which have been implicitly formed. Such is the wish and the goal of what to be realized of the laboratory itself.
4 By realized world, we note that the word world in particular is often overloaded with meanings. In retrospect, one can have the phase world (space), which already presupposes a specific form of encoding to express the expression thereof relevant to the properties or description desired, a proxical world where it is an idealized setting of a more complex situation, and then the physical world where the physical manifestation and existential condition is forced (i.e. instead of infinite apples, you have finite \(n\) apples instead). Such would also be representative of what the laboratory would study as a topic, because while saying such, we are not satisfied by philosophical talk, but also unsatisfied of the technical jargon either.
0.1 The general theoretical-empirical research
The posture that MTAIL wants to equip itself with, under investigation, and in build-up for RHINELAB, can be perhaps minimally expressed of the following points. Note that they function mostly, or rather deliberately like an assertions list, less than typically what to be ‘study and go’, perspectively. That said, if to summarize it in a few parts, such would be that we aim to formalize and research of everything from scratch, of each assumption, each choice, of all the historical records and evolution, of all logical lines of evolution and not just the end results, and even more so the entire field of its open problem and the load-bearing pillars that are scaffolding the entire modern system of studies.
Why, would it be so of a decision template, or rather to pursue such interest? Why would it not be easier to stand on the shoulder of the giants and forever holding such order of authority without knowing? Would it be so satisfying as to never question the ground, be it for good or for bad, be it for change or for resolution, for the search of something or the excavation of the past, be it so, now that cowering into a corner of obsession with hedging, the culture of which we are to believe that we have known everything, saying in passing, while simultaneously believing that we do? We ought, at least of MTAIL and the wider RHINELAB, not to follow such line of argument and thought of work, be it so passing by of convenience, be comfort the enemy of real thoughts, and only genuine thoughts as unconventional and unsatisfying as it is, be the honest one. Let us build and analyze from the ground up. Build the theory, the pre-theory, the system, the way to analyze, all the way to the top, all the way to the side, to see the assumption, to the logical process, to situate oneself in the process of revolution or progress in what to be of concerned of science, because for once scientists are all but mortals, and the giants were once nobody. Let us see through and build everything, even with a manual, yet to understand and fully appreciate it, rather than simplify it, hedging it until where we see our ends, or neglect it away. Let us see what theory is, and to see of which empirical be, not just the word, the simple definition but the comparison and structure thereof. In a sense, what to ask of MTAIL, is to devise and to create the bodies of works, that focus on the art of building knowledge, building science, building theories and the opposition thereof, the stack of pre-theory constructs and statements that come before any theory comes to fruition or statements; and last of all, from the anthropology, to live in such process, framework and philosophy. This, includes mathematics, includes all form of sciences and theoretical studies, and the way each of the theories are formed of their load-bearing nodes.
Poetic as it might sound, and philosophical as it might get, the point is simple: we are in the period of many information. We are in the time when knowledge proliferation is not exquisite virtue but real access. Where theories and knowledge has been built substantially. MTAIL simply seeks to analyze this in full. That, and the more theoretical and imaginative part of theoretical studies. Because man once dream, and Icarus once soared. Where he felt, he smiles because he knows he tried. Of the imagination that catches our wing, be it broken and never realized, let it be that our mind have tried, not to look above and stare at the dazzling sun without reach. MTAIL exists to study what it means to build knowledge — rigorously, historically, structurally, and from the inside — across every domain RHINELAB touches. Such is also why, don’t ask when we cover a lot of fields.
After that, what to be illustrated of such? Many of those points will be repeated later, but let us try to attempt doing so right now, as the prescription downward.
First, is one of the direct address of what we dub as the theoretical-practical gap, between theory and practices. (TBD, I will write more later)

title: Example and formatting
text: This one is taken in consideration of the demonstration needed to show how this template would work with markdown syntax, since each template and any given modification changes how the web browser engine works and design them at all. The original one is taken from here.

title: Example and formatting
text:
1.1 Overview

1.1.1 Philosophy
Markdown is intended to be as easy-to-read and easy-to-write as is feasible.
Readability, however, is emphasized above all else. A Markdown-formatted document should be publishable as-is, as plain text, without looking like it’s been marked up with tags or formatting instructions. While Markdown’s syntax has been influenced by several existing text-to-HTML filters – including Setext, atx, Textile, reStructuredText, Grutatext, and EtText – the single biggest source of inspiration for Markdown’s syntax is the format of plain text email.

title: Example and formatting
text:
1.2 Block Elements

1.2.1 Paragraphs and Line Breaks
A paragraph is simply one or more consecutive lines of text, separated by one or more blank lines. (A blank line is any line that looks like a blank line – a line containing nothing but spaces or tabs is considered blank.) Normal paragraphs should not be indented with spaces or tabs.
The implication of the “one or more consecutive lines of text” rule is that Markdown supports “hard-wrapped” text paragraphs. This differs significantly from most other text-to-HTML formatters (including Movable Type’s “Convert Line Breaks” option) which translate every line break character in a paragraph into a <br /> tag.
When you do want to insert a <br /> break tag using Markdown, you end a line with two or more spaces, then type return.


1.2.2 Headers
Markdown supports two styles of headers, [Setext] [1] and [atx] [2].
Optionally, you may “close” atx-style headers. This is purely cosmetic – you can use this if you think it looks better. The closing hashes don’t even need to match the number of hashes used to open the header. (The number of opening hashes determines the header level.)


1.2.3 Blockquotes
Markdown uses email-style > characters for blockquoting. If you’re familiar with quoting passages of text in an email message, then you know how to create a blockquote in Markdown. It looks best if you hard wrap the text and put a > before every line:

This is a blockquote with two paragraphs. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit. Aliquam hendrerit mi posuere lectus. Vestibulum enim wisi, viverra nec, fringilla in, laoreet vitae, risus.
Donec sit amet nisl. Aliquam semper ipsum sit amet velit. Suspendisse id sem consectetuer libero luctus adipiscing.

Markdown allows you to be lazy and only put the > before the first line of a hard-wrapped paragraph:

This is a blockquote with two paragraphs. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit. Aliquam hendrerit mi posuere lectus. Vestibulum enim wisi, viverra nec, fringilla in, laoreet vitae, risus.


Donec sit amet nisl. Aliquam semper ipsum sit amet velit. Suspendisse id sem consectetuer libero luctus adipiscing.

Blockquotes can be nested (i.e. a blockquote-in-a-blockquote) by adding additional levels of >:

This is the first level of quoting.

This is nested blockquote.

Back to the first level.

Blockquotes can contain other Markdown elements, including headers, lists, and code blocks:

1.3 This is a header.

This is the first list item.
This is the second list item.

Here’s some example code:
return shell_exec("echo $input | $markdown_script");

Any decent text editor should make email-style quoting easy. For example, with BBEdit, you can make a selection and choose Increase Quote Level from the Text menu.


1.3.1 Lists
Markdown supports ordered (numbered) and unordered (bulleted) lists.
Unordered lists use asterisks, pluses, and hyphens – interchangably – as list markers:

Red
Green
Blue

is equivalent to:

Red
Green
Blue

and:

Red
Green
Blue

Ordered lists use numbers followed by periods:

Bird
McHale
Parish

It’s important to note that the actual numbers you use to mark the list have no effect on the HTML output Markdown produces. The HTML Markdown produces from the above list is:
If you instead wrote the list in Markdown like this:

Bird
McHale
Parish

or even:

Bird
McHale
Parish

you’d get the exact same HTML output. The point is, if you want to, you can use ordinal numbers in your ordered Markdown lists, so that the numbers in your source match the numbers in your published HTML. But if you want to be lazy, you don’t have to.
To make lists look nice, you can wrap items with hanging indents:

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit. Aliquam hendrerit mi posuere lectus. Vestibulum enim wisi, viverra nec, fringilla in, laoreet vitae, risus.
Donec sit amet nisl. Aliquam semper ipsum sit amet velit. Suspendisse id sem consectetuer libero luctus adipiscing.

But if you want to be lazy, you don’t have to:

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit. Aliquam hendrerit mi posuere lectus. Vestibulum enim wisi, viverra nec, fringilla in, laoreet vitae, risus.
Donec sit amet nisl. Aliquam semper ipsum sit amet velit. Suspendisse id sem consectetuer libero luctus adipiscing.

List items may consist of multiple paragraphs. Each subsequent paragraph in a list item must be indented by either 4 spaces or one tab:

This is a list item with two paragraphs. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit. Aliquam hendrerit mi posuere lectus.
Vestibulum enim wisi, viverra nec, fringilla in, laoreet vitae, risus. Donec sit amet nisl. Aliquam semper ipsum sit amet velit.
Suspendisse id sem consectetuer libero luctus adipiscing.

It looks nice if you indent every line of the subsequent paragraphs, but here again, Markdown will allow you to be lazy:

This is a list item with two paragraphs.
This is the second paragraph in the list item. You’re only required to indent the first line. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetuer adipiscing elit.
Another item in the same list.

To put a blockquote within a list item, the blockquote’s > delimiters need to be indented:

A list item with a blockquote:

This is a blockquote inside a list item.


To put a code block within a list item, the code block needs to be indented twice – 8 spaces or two tabs:

A list item with a code block:
<code goes here>



1.3.2 Code Blocks
Pre-formatted code blocks are used for writing about programming or markup source code. Rather than forming normal paragraphs, the lines of a code block are interpreted literally. Markdown wraps a code block in both <pre> and <code> tags.
To produce a code block in Markdown, simply indent every line of the block by at least 4 spaces or 1 tab.
This is a normal paragraph:
This is a code block.
Here is an example of AppleScript:
tell application "Foo"
    beep
end tell
A code block continues until it reaches a line that is not indented (or the end of the article).
Within a code block, ampersands (&) and angle brackets (< and >) are automatically converted into HTML entities. This makes it very easy to include example HTML source code using Markdown – just paste it and indent it, and Markdown will handle the hassle of encoding the ampersands and angle brackets. For example, this:
<div class="footer">
    © 2004 Foo Corporation
</div>
Regular Markdown syntax is not processed within code blocks. E.g., asterisks are just literal asterisks within a code block. This means it’s also easy to use Markdown to write about Markdown’s own syntax.
tell application "Foo"
    beep
end tell

title: Example and formatting
text:
1.4 Span Elements

1.4.1 Links
Markdown supports two style of links: inline and reference.
In both styles, the link text is delimited by [square brackets].
To create an inline link, use a set of regular parentheses immediately after the link text’s closing square bracket. Inside the parentheses, put the URL where you want the link to point, along with an optional title for the link, surrounded in quotes. For example:
This is an example inline link.
This link has no title attribute.


1.4.2 Emphasis
Markdown treats asterisks (*) and underscores (_) as indicators of emphasis. Text wrapped with one * or _ will be wrapped with an HTML <em> tag; double *’s or _’s will be wrapped with an HTML <strong> tag. E.g., this input:
single asterisks
single underscores
double asterisks
double underscores


1.4.3 Code
To indicate a span of code, wrap it with backtick quotes (`). Unlike a pre-formatted code block, a code span indicates code within a normal paragraph. For example:
Use the printf() function.
